kleśa
(‘that which produces pain and sorrow’)
------------------------------------------
Though this word means a problem or a difficulty that produces sorrow and suffering, the Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) uses this word as a technical term (vide 2.3; 1.24). Traced from the root-verb ‘kliś’ it means anything that causes sorrow, suffering and bondage.
The kleśas are five in number. They are: अविद्या (nescience), अस्मिता (ego-sense), राग (attachment), द्वेष (hatred, aversion) and अभिनिवेश (excessive attachment to life, fear of death).
They can be eliminated by meditation on the आत्मन् (the Self) and ultimately by the dissolution of the चित्त or the मिन्द्, in its cause, the प्रधान (insentient material cause of the whole च्रेअतिओन्).
